original_paper_citation: Shi et al. (NeurIPS 2015), 'Convolutional LSTM Network: A Machine Learning Approach for Precipitation Nowcasting'
original_architecture_or_algorithm: 2-layer recurrent sequence-to-sequence ConvLSTM cell where matrix multiplications in input/forget/output gates are replaced by 2D spatial convolution operators (W * X + U * H + b). Uses recurrent encoder-decoder unrolling.
key_architectural_differences: Our model retains the exact gate convolution mathematics of Shi et al., but replaces the recurrent autoregressive decoder with 5 parallel multi-horizon convolutional prediction heads (+30m, +60m, +120m, +180m, +360m). Platt scaling is added to calibrate probabilities.
dataset_and_input_adaptation: Shi et al. trained on Hong Kong Observatory (HKO-7) radar reflectivity (480x480, 6-min cadence, 1 km). Our implementation adapts to multi-sensor satellite data: 4 km MERGIR IR (Tb) + 0.1 deg IMERG rain rate on a 25x40 common grid over Meghalaya.
fairness_of_comparison: FAIR: Evaluated on identical held-out test frames (July 6–7, 2025, N=85,000 pixels) and identical 5.0 mm/hr threshold as all baselines.
scientific_validation_notes: Core ConvLSTM gate cell is mathematically identical to Shi et al. Eq. 1-6. Multi-head output allows simultaneous direct evaluation across 5 lead times without compounding autoregressive error.

original_paper_citation: Ayzel et al. (GMD 2019), 'rainymotion v0.1: a Python library for radar-based precipitation nowcasting based on optical flow techniques'
original_architecture_or_algorithm: Dense optical flow tracking (DisFlow / Farneback) calculating motion vector field (u, v) between consecutive frames, followed by Semi-Lagrangian backward advection extrapolation with linear persistence hold.
key_architectural_differences: Implements dense Lucas-Kanade optical flow gradients via SciPy/NumPy rather than OpenCV DisFlow. Extrapolation uses genuine Semi-Lagrangian backward coordinate mapping with bilinear interpolation.
dataset_and_input_adaptation: Original rainymotion was designed for German Weather Service (DWD) RADOLAN ground radar composites (900x900, 5-min, 1 km). Adapted here to 0.1 deg IMERG satellite precipitation fields at 30-min cadence.
fairness_of_comparison: FAIR: Ingests the exact same past two half-hourly precipitation frames and predicts identical lead steps (1, 2, 4, 6, 12) on identical held-out grids.
scientific_validation_notes: Faithfully reproduces the kinematic Semi-Lagrangian advection principle of Ayzel et al. Proves that optical flow matches ConvLSTM for 30 min but degrades at longer horizons due to inability to simulate cloud dissipation/growth.

paper_method: Gradient Boosted Decision Trees for Terrain Susceptibility
original_paper_citation: Chen & Guestrin (KDD 2016), 'XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System'
original_architecture_or_algorithm: Exact and weighted quantile sketch gradient boosting with second-order Taylor expansion of the objective function, column subsampling, shrinkage, and tree pruning.
key_architectural_differences: Uses official XGBoost engine implementing Chen & Guestrin's exact loss formulations (max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.8, objective='binary:logistic').
dataset_and_input_adaptation: Adapted from general tabular datasets to 90 m SRTM digital elevation morphometry (elevation, slope, aspect sin/cos, plan curvature, profile curvature).
fairness_of_comparison: FAIR: Evaluated under strict 3-fold spatial block cross-validation (West Garo, Central Khasi, East Jaintia) with identical symmetric feature extraction for landslide and background points.
scientific_validation_notes: Authentic execution of Chen & Guestrin (2016). Removed previous asymmetric 450m scarp-max sampling artifact; honest symmetric spatial cross-validation yields mean ROC-AUC of 0.5913.

paper_method: Post-Hoc Probability Calibration via Logistic Scaling
original_paper_citation: Platt (Adv Large Margin Classifiers 1999), 'Probabilistic Outputs for Support Vector Machines and Comparisons to Regularized Likelihood Methods'
original_architecture_or_algorithm: Fits a 2-parameter univariate logistic sigmoid P(y=1|z) = 1 / (1 + exp(-(a*z + b))) to uncalibrated margin/logits z using maximum likelihood on a held-out calibration set.
key_architectural_differences: Implemented via scikit-learn LogisticRegression(solver='lbfgs') on 1D validation logits. Fitted parameters a=0.9703, b=-3.0935 neutralize the +3.0 logit shift from weighted BCE loss.
dataset_and_input_adaptation: Adapted to spatiotemporal ConvLSTM logits for precipitation occurrence (>= 5.0 mm/hr). Fitted strictly on validation period (July 5, 2025); evaluated on test set (July 6–7, 2025).
fairness_of_comparison: FAIR: Strictly separated calibration from test evaluation. Demonstrates out-of-sample Brier score reduction from 0.0322 to 0.0083 (-74.3%).
scientific_validation_notes: Exact reproduction of Platt's parametric calibration formulation. Solves the uncalibrated over-forecasting anomaly while strictly preserving discrimination rank.

paper_method: Dynamic Antecedent Rainfall Hazard Decision Matrix
original_paper_citation: Stanley et al. (Frontiers Earth Sci 2021), 'Data-Driven Landslide Hazard Assessment at Global Scale with LHASA-Version 2'; Kirschbaum & Stanley (2018)
original_architecture_or_algorithm: Global dynamic landslide hazard framework combining a static susceptibility map with antecedent rainfall index (ARI) via an empirical decision matrix or machine-learned heuristic into categorical hazard levels.
key_architectural_differences: Our implementation is a regional heuristic Antecedent Rainfall Index decision matrix coupling 90m SRTM LSI with IMERG antecedent rainfall (A = 0.6*P_24h + 0.4*P_72h). It is NOT an exact reproduction of the global machine-learned LHASA 2.0 system.
dataset_and_input_adaptation: Stanley et al. used global IMERG daily rainfall, global SRTM slope, forest loss, and geological maps. We adapted the concept to regional 0.1 deg IMERG half-hourly series and 90m SRTM terrain over Meghalaya.
fairness_of_comparison: FAIR_CONCEPTUAL_HEURISTIC: Clearly identified as a custom heuristic decision matrix inspired by LHASA principles, not an exact model clone.
scientific_validation_notes: Maintains dual independent paradigm: weather and landslide layers are combined through a transparent decision matrix rather than invalid joint-probability multiplication.
